source_row.stem: A nurse explains that cervical cancer screening intervals may be extended when HPV testing is combined with Pap testing, known as co-testing, and a client assumes combining two tests would only make sense if it meant screening needed to happen more often, not less. The nurse explains that this is instead because:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Co-testing with a negative result provides higher confidence in ruling out significant risk, supporting longer intervals between screenings, rather than more frequent screening as the client is currently assuming","B":"Co-testing is considered to add fairly little additional value over Pap testing alone when assessing a client's cervical cancer risk, contrary to why this combined approach actually extends the interval","C":"Co-testing is reserved mainly for clients already considered high-risk, rather than offered as part of routine average-risk screening like this client is receiving","D":"The screening interval is kept roughly the same length regardless of which specific testing method a client's screening happens to be based on, contrary to why combining tests actually changes the interval"}}
source_row.rationale: When HPV co-testing is combined with Pap testing and both are negative, this combination provides higher confidence in ruling out significant cervical cancer risk, supporting longer intervals between screenings per current guidelines.
